main_body: Three-storey red brick building facade with a large flat grey roof slab on top, rows of white-framed windows, and a green arched double door
top_band: Light lavender-grey roof surface, rows ~2-38 (about 36 rows), with a lighter front-edge highlight at rows ~36-38 and cream cornice below at rows ~40-46
evidence: Column read at mid-body: the roof is a large flat grey stone-textured slab (rows 2-38) with chimneys/vents standing on it, ending in a light front-edge line (rows ~36-38). Below it a cream cornice band (rows ~40-46) and a dark shadow row sit above the brick wall (rows ~47-138). Windows have cream sills and lintels, and the door has an arched fanlight with inset frames. The roof is a real horizontal surface seen from above with the front wall below. It is tall relative to the wall (36 vs 96 rows), but it reads as a flat roof seen from above, with rooftop objects confirming the top view. Passes as 3/4.

style.evidence: The brick wall has several red-brown tones with brick-by-brick variation and mortar rows. The cream trim carries 3-4 steps. The roof has speckled stone texture with panel seams and a lighter edge. Windows show glass with blue/teal variation and reflection dots. The outlines are dark red-brown beside brick and dark tinted tones beside the trim, not pure black. Detail density per tile is high, comparable to the Beodeul references. The roof is somewhat uniform but speckled, so no large flat fills.
